lawyer:
Gazi Siddique Ahmed, Advocate—For the Appellant. 
Md Ibrahim Khalil, Assistant Attorney-General—For the Respondent.
parties:
Ali Hossain alias Ali ------ Appellant
vs
State ------ Respondents.
full_judgment: 27. On critical analysis of the case it appears that PW 4 Monowara Khatun, mother of the victim and PW 6 victim Rubina Akter are the eye-witnesses of the occurrence. Rest of the local witnesses rushed to the scene after the explosion and heard of the occurrence from PW 4 Monowara Khatun. It appears from the evidence of PW 4 Monowara Khatun that on 7-10-1989 at 3-30 PM she found her daughter PW 6 victim Rubina was unsuccessfully trying to open a small tin pot of zorda which she (PW 6) collected from their nearby brick stock. The slain Awlad also participated to open it. The accused Ali Hossain suddenly happened there and took away the pot. Then the victim Rubina went inside the hut. Accused hurled the said tin pot aiming at them which exploded inside the hut of Anowar Hossain causing injuries upon the person of slain Awlad and PW 6 Rubina who was also wounded. Subsequently, Awlad succumbed to the injuries at Mitford Medical College Hospital. PW 6 Rubina Akter also corroborated the facts and manner of occurrence with the PW 4 Monowara Khatun. Their evidence regarding taking away the tin pot and throwing the same aiming at them are consistent and uniform and soon after the occurrence the matter was disclosed to the locals by her (PW 4) and the same was corroborated by the other witnesses. So, there is no reason to disbelieve them although they were extensively cross-examined by the defence but nothing was elicited to shake their credibility. It further appears from the evidence of PWs 4 and 6 that certainly without any premeditated motive the accused Ali Hossain happened to the spot and curiously took away the tin pot from the slain Awlad and there is no evidence that the accused carried the said tin pot and he had any knowledge about components/ingredients inside the tin pot. There is also no evidence that the accused had any knowledge about the consequence of throwing the tin pot. But the fact remains that tin pot exploded, subsequently Awlad Hossain succumbed to the injuries caused by the explosive substance and PW 6 Rubina Akter was also wounded. So, having regard to the fact we are of the view that even if an act by the accused resulting in death is admitted, there can be no presumption that the act was voluntary and intentional and these elements must be established by the prosecution, like any other element of the offence charged. It is not correct to say that the accused must be found guilty if he fails to show the circumstances necessary to establish the accident pleaded by him. With this regard, reliance can be placed in the case of Sultan Muhammad vs Crown reported in 6 DLR (FC) 28. It is also held in the case of State vs Ashraf Ali and others reported in 1994 BLD (AD) 127 that mere killing of a person or mere causing a person's death is not murder, culpable homicide or even any criminal offence but it is so when caused with certain guilty intention or guilty knowledge. Three classes of cases have been described in section 299 of the Penal Code as "culpable homicide" and four classes of cases have been described in section 300 as "murder". The essential difference between mere "culpable homicide" and "murder" is the degree of probability of causing death. When death is probable, it is culpable homicide but when death is most probable, it is murder. So in the facts and circumstances of the case we are of the view that act was done within the knowledge that it is likely to cause death. But without intention to cause death or to cause such bodily injury as to cause death which will come within the mischief of section 304 Part II of the Penal Code and, as such, the appellant ought to have been convicted under section 304 Part II of the Penal Code. But the learned Judge of the trial Court wrongly convicted him under section 302 of the Penal Code.
